full_judgment:
Mr. Sharif Uddin Chaklader, J: By this rule, the accused petitioners challenged the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 1966 of 2005 under section 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. The complainant opposite party. Mohammad Amir All Mostofa, in his petition of complaint alleges that the case property was originally allotted to Md. Musa Khan and lease deed was executed and lease deed No.6759 dated 27.2.196I was registered in favour of said Md. Musa Khan, Musa Khan transferred the case property to Mustari Begum the mother of the complainant on 10.6.1970 and mutated her name and got a plan passed from D.I.T. and constituted two stored building as per said plan and thereafter, gifted the said property to the complainant and his two sisters on 5.9.2005. While the complainant and his two sisters possessed the said property, on 2.11.2005, 5/6 young men entered into the said house forcefully and took away the complainant and his father on a microbus and after sometime of the said abduction, the Chairman of the Mercantile Bank Limited along with some officials of the said Bank, came to the case land and declared that they have purchased the disputed property. At 7.30 p.m. of the same dated the complainant and his father were released and thereafter, the mother of the complainant lodged the F.I.R. with Gulshan Police Station on 2.11.2005. On 3.11.2005 an advertisement was published by the accused No.2 in daily Star stated that they have purchased the disputed property. The Complainant obtained certified copy of the said purchased deed and came to know that the accused’s in collusion with each other has obtained the said deed by false personification of the real owner, Mushtari Begum, the mother of the complainant. Thereafter, the complainant made the petition of complaint. 

 3. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka by order dated 9.11.2005 sent the Complaint for judicial inquiry and after getting the report of the judicial inquiry, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka took cognizance against the accused petitioners on 7.3.2006. The accused petitioners, at first, obtained bail from this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3923 of 2006 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case, No.4317 of 2007 and thereafter, they obtained regular bail from the learned Magistrate. 

 4. Mr. M. Ziaul Hasan with Mr. Mr. K.M. Salauddin, learned Advocates, submits that, although a proceeding should not be quashed before framing of charge but the learned Advocate submits that, when the proceeding is barred under law and also that the facts of the proceeding give rise to civil litigation then the proceeding can be quashed before framing of charge. Learned Advocate further submits that, this proceeding is barred under two counts as such learned Advocate further submits that, at this stage of the case the proceeding can be quashed. Learned Advocate further submits that, over the self same deed, two civil Suits being Title Suit No.504 of 2005 and Title Suit No.1 of 2006, one by the complainant and another by the accused petitioners, are pending before the competent civil Court where the sent centered round the impugned deed of the instant proceeding and the declaration sought for in respect of the instant deed, as such, if the suit, be decreed or dismissed, then the concerned court is competent to lodged the proceeding under section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in that view of the matter this proceeding has no leg to stand, as such, the instant proceeding is liable to be quashed. 

 6. Motijheel Police Station investigated the case and on 26.5.2006 submitted final report. From annexure D, it appears that Mercantile Bank Limited instituted Title Suit NO.504 of 2005 on 30.11.2005 alleging the same fact and praying for declaration of the title in respect of the case property and also for a declaration that; 

 7. From annexure E it appears that the complainant with his two sisters as plaintiffy instituted Title Suit No.1 of 2006 for declaration of title in respect of the case property with the other declarations that; 

 It appears that over the self same deed two suits one by the accused petitioner and another by the complainant are pending before the Civil Court. The suits are subsequent to lodging. of the complaint but in the complaint it appears that charge has not yet been framed and as per decision of Mohitullah Pk. Alias Mohitullah and others versus The State, reported in 38 DLR (AD) 241 and Md. Alam Vs. State, reported in 19 DLR (SC) 268, the instant Criminal Proceeding can not be said to be pending for trial. It appears from the declaration sought for in both the civil suits that the deed upon which the accused petitioners purchased the case property of the instant criminal case whether genuine or not. If the suit be decreed or dismissed in both counts the instant proceeding is barred under section 195 of the Code of Civil Procedure as if the civil Court declared the deed of the accused petitioners is genuine and then also this proceeding is barred as in that case the question of forgery does not arise and if the civil Court declared the deed of the accused petitioner the false and product of forgery in that case the proceeding of the instant case is barred as in that case Court is competent under the provision of section 195 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to lodged a complaint for using forged document before a competent Court. 

 8. Learned Advocate for the accused petitioner relied on the decision of Executive Engineer, Water Development Board and another vs. Md. Moktaruddin and others, reported in 11 BLC (AD) 32. On the facts of the given case we are of the view this decision at present is not applicable. Learned Advocate also relied on the decision Abdur Rahman Vs. State reported in 59 DLR-683 wherein it has been a Division Bench of this Court relied on the decision Abdul Hai Khan vs. State reported in 40 DLR (AD) 22.6, Md. Tokumuddin Par vs. State 1996 BLT (AD) 14, Nur Ahmed vs. Kalimuddin 1987 BCR (AD) 152, Raja Kushal Pal Singh, AIR 1961 ALL-443. It has been held that since the alleged forged document has been filed in the civil Court which is the subject matter of a suit for Specific Performance of Contract, it is for the concerned civil Court to lodge any complaint before the criminal Court if it finds the forgery relating to the said document. But the instant proceeding in C.R. Case No. 1966 of 2005 under section 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code has been initiated on private complaint the same cannot continue in view of the provision of section 195(1)(C) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. We find substance in this rule. 

 10. The proceeding of C.R. Case No.1966 of 2005 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. Dhaka is quashed so far as it relates to the accused petitioners.
